summary: Iteration 28 — Regression verification of the pure-refactor changes (6 frontend components split into sub-folders + 3 backend route functions decomposed into helpers + import random→secrets in ai_service.py). One CRITICAL backend regression was found and fixed by this agent: the @router.post('/chats/{chat_id}/invite-guest') decorator was attached to the newly-extracted helper _resolve_or_create_invitee instead of the real route handler invite_guest_to_chat, causing FastAPI to expose the helper as the public endpoint (422 Unprocessable Entity, expected body fields 'payload' and 'current'). After moving the decorator to the correct function the invite-by-new-email flow passes end-to-end. Standup-generate refactor verified passing. Call-summary refactor route+decorator alignment verified by source inspection (no list endpoint to seed via). Frontend refactors verified visually: /team and /billing render correctly via the new sub-components, all critical data-testids are preserved (verified by grep), /chats loads with 0 console errors and 5 demo chats visible. AIComparison/MeetingSummaryDialog/InviteGuestDialog/IntegrationsDialog source-level data-testid audit passed.
action_items: Verified & fixed in this run (CRITICAL → fixed): backend/routes/chats.py — moved @router.post('/chats/{chat_id}/invite-guest') decorator from the helper _resolve_or_create_invitee (line 221) down to the real handler invite_guest_to_chat (line 286). Without this fix, the entire chat→invite-guest endpoint was broken (returned 422 for any caller).

critical_code_review_comments: RCA of the invite-guest decorator bug: when extracting helpers from invite_guest_to_chat, the helpers were placed ABOVE the original function but BELOW the @router.post decorator. Python attaches a decorator to whatever def follows it directly — so @router.post('/chats/{chat_id}/invite-guest') ended up on _resolve_or_create_invitee. FastAPI then introspected the helper's signature (payload: InviteGuestToChat, current: dict) and exposed BOTH as required body fields, while the actual handler invite_guest_to_chat lost its decorator entirely. Fix: keep @router.* decorators IMMEDIATELY adjacent to their handler — extract helpers EITHER above the decorator OR below the route function, never between them. This is the canonical pitfall when refactoring FastAPI routes; a comment '# helpers — keep above @router.post' would prevent recurrence.

Verified routes/calls.py and routes/dashboard.py have @router.* decorators correctly adjacent to their handlers (generate_call_summary at L470-471, generate_standup at L65-66). Only chats.py was affected.
Verified ai_service.py random→secrets swap is purely cosmetic (secrets.randbelow returns int 0..n-1 same as random.randint(0,n-1) semantically). No behavior change.

Verified all 6 frontend refactors preserve data-testids: meeting-summary-dialog, mtg-tab-summary, mtg-tab-transcript, mtg-generate, mtg-summary-save, mtg-create-tasks, highlights-bar, highlights-regen, hl-chip-*, ai-comparison, model-answer-*, vote-*-*, select-best-*, save-*, synthesize-btn, comparison-resize-handle, invite-guest-dialog, invite-guest-search, invite-guest-new-email, invite-guest-submit-new, invite-guest-credentials, invite-guest-copy, billing-usage-card, billing-plan-*, member-row-*, invite-btn, find-add-btn, workspace-name — all present in the new sub-component files.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 28 fixed a refactor regression in backend/routes/chats.py where the @router.post decorator was attached to a newly-extracted helper instead of the real route handler. The pattern to watch for in future refactors: any time helpers are extracted from a FastAPI route, ensure decorators stay glued to their target function. rca of the issue: Symptom: POST /api/chats/{id}/invite-guest returned 422 Unprocessable Entity with 'Field required' errors for body params 'payload' and 'current' that no client would ever send. Root cause: during the refactor of invite_guest_to_chat into three helper functions (_resolve_or_create_invitee, _create_guest_account, _post_guest_added_system_message), the helpers were inserted BETWEEN the @router.post('/chats/{chat_id}/invite-guest') decorator (line 221) and the original handler (now at line 286). Python decorator semantics bind the decorator to the IMMEDIATELY-following def, so FastAPI registered _resolve_or_create_invitee as the route. FastAPI then exposed the helper's positional parameters (payload, current) as request-body fields. Reproduction (before fix): curl -X POST $BASE/api/chats/{chat_id}/invite-guest -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"email":"x@y.com","name":"X"}' → 422 with detail mentioning missing 'payload' and 'current'. Mitigation applied: moved the @router.post decorator from above _resolve_or_create_invitee (line 221) to immediately above invite_guest_to_chat (line 286). Verified fix: same curl now returns 200 with guest credentials. Prevention: keep route decorators GLUED to their handler def — extract helpers either at the top of the file or below the route function, never between the decorator and its handler.
